investigations.name: annealing
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 2+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=2, J_dd=2, J_ld=2, J_lM=8, J_dM=8 (gamma_ld=+0, gamma_lM=+7, gamma_dM=+7); T=0.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_light. Figures reproduced: Fig 2, Fig 3.
investigations.title: Annealing convergence
investigations.objective: Does the pattern's topology (<n>, moments) converge within a few MCS of T=0 annealing, as in Glazier-Graner Fig 2-3?
investigations.claim: Bulk <n> converges to ~5.97 within ~2 MCS with total<bulk, reproducing Fig 2; cell walls compact by 2-20 MCS (Fig 3).

investigations.name: cell_sorting
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 12+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 12, Fig 13, Fig 14, Fig 15, Fig 16, Table II, Table III.
investigations.title: Cell sorting
investigations.objective: Does differential adhesion (gamma_dM>gamma_lM>gamma_ld>0) sort a random mix into dark-inside / light-monolayer, as observed by Armstrong and Steinberg?
investigations.claim: Complete cell sorting: dark cells cluster internally beneath a light monolayer; heterotypic contact falls while light-medium contact rises, reproducing Figs 12-16 and Tables II-III.

investigations.name: checkerboard
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 7+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=10, J_dd=8, J_ld=6, J_lM=12, J_dM=12 (gamma_ld=-3, gamma_lM=+7, gamma_dM=+8); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 7, Fig 8, Fig 9, Table I.
investigations.title: Checkerboard (negative surface tension)
investigations.objective: Does a negative light-dark surface tension (gamma_ld=-3) drive intermixing into a checkerboard instead of sorting?
investigations.claim: gamma_ld<0 yields a defect-ridden checkerboard with dominant light-dark contact and two transitions (~T=0 freeze, ~T=15 mixing), matching Figs 7-9 and Table I.

investigations.name: dispersal_no_separate
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 27+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=29, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+21, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 27.
investigations.title: Dispersal - clusters do not separate
investigations.objective: At gamma_ld=21, do light/dark clusters stay attached (extreme partial sorting) rather than fully separate?
investigations.claim: Clusters remain attached, an extreme partial-sorting case just below the separation threshold (Fig 27).

investigations.name: dispersal_separate
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 26+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=35, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+27, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 26.
investigations.title: Dispersal - clusters separate
investigations.objective: Does a very high heterotypic tension (gamma_ld=27) make light and dark clusters fully separate?
investigations.claim: Light and dark clusters separate completely; a few isolated dark cells occur (Fig 26).

investigations.name: dispersal_sloughing
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 25+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=4, J_ld=11, J_lM=2, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+2, gamma_lM=-5, gamma_dM=+14); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 25.
investigations.title: Dispersal - light-cell sloughing
investigations.objective: Does a negative light-Medium tension (gamma_lM=-5) make light cells slough off and disperse into the medium?
investigations.claim: Light cells disperse as isolated cells into the medium while dark cells remain compact and round (Fig 25).

investigations.name: engulfment
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 18+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: half_split. Figures reproduced: Fig 18, Fig 19.
investigations.title: Engulfment
investigations.objective: Does an initially half-light/half-dark aggregate engulf to the same sorted configuration as the random-IC sort?
investigations.claim: Light cells engulf the dark mass and the final state matches the random-IC sort, confirming initial-condition independence (Figs 18-19).

investigations.name: global_equilibration
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 4+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=2, J_dd=2, J_ld=2, J_lM=8, J_dM=8 (gamma_ld=+0, gamma_lM=+7, gamma_dM=+7); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: brick_equilibrate. Figures reproduced: Fig 4, Fig 5.
investigations.title: Global pattern equilibration
investigations.objective: Does a rectangular brick tiling relax into a rounded, topologically-equilibrated aggregate at T=5?
investigations.claim: The tiling rounds into a 1012-cell disk with <n>~6.0, mu2~0.69, matching Fig 4b; statistics stable after ~400 MCS (Fig 5).

investigations.name: partial_sorting
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 22+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=11, J_dd=2, J_ld=14, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+7.5, gamma_lM=+10.5, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 22, Fig 23, Fig 24.
investigations.title: Partial cell sorting
investigations.objective: Does violating the Young condition (large gamma_ld=7.5) stall sorting at a partially-sorted, trapped state?
investigations.claim: Sorting stalls partial: no light monolayer forms and clusters trap inclusions, markedly slower than normal sorting (Figs 22-24).

investigations.name: position_reversal
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 20+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=30, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+23, gamma_dM=+15); T=10.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=40.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 20, Fig 21.
investigations.title: Position reversal
investigations.objective: Does raising the light-Medium tension (gamma_lM=23) reverse the sorting so dark cells end up outside?
investigations.claim: Dark cells sort OUTWARD, surrounding the light cells, the reversed pattern predicted for gamma_lM>gamma_dM (Figs 20-21).

investigations.name: recruitment-adversarial
investigations.description:
The adversarial / negative-control arm. Responders are fully competent (lambda=14)
but there is no cue (secretion rate 0), so no gradient forms. A trustworthy
recruitment claim must FAIL to fire here — the metric passes by rejecting a system
that should not qualify. This closes the causal logic: recruitment requires BOTH a
cue AND a response, and neither alone suffices.
investigations.title: Control: no cue, no recruitment
investigations.objective:
If competent responders are placed with NO cue secreted, does the metric
correctly report no recruitment (rather than a spurious signal)?
investigations.claim:
Without a cue, competent responders are not recruited: the recruitment index
stays at 0. The metric does not produce a false-positive recruitment signal.

investigations.name: recruitment-baseline
investigations.description:
The anchoring positive condition of the chemotactic-recruitment slice. Type-1
source cells secrete field C (d=0.22, decay=0.001); type-2 responders start ~33 px
away and chemotax up the gradient with strength lambda=14. This is the native
viva-cpm realization of the biological claim "a secreted cue recruits responder
cells", and the ground-truth study the Biological Claim Layer compiler must
reproduce.
investigations.title: Baseline: cue + response recruits
investigations.objective:
When source cells secrete a diffusible cue and responder cells carry a
competent chemotactic response, do the responders directionally migrate up the
gradient and accumulate at the source?
investigations.claim:
Responders climb the secreted gradient and are recruited to the source: the
recruitment index rises from 0 to a plateau of ~0.67-0.83 (mean approach 0.61).

investigations.name: recruitment-inhibited
investigations.description:
The intervention arm of the slice. The world is identical to the baseline except
the responder chemotaxis lambda is set to 0 — the CPM analogue of pharmacologically
blocking the receptor/response while the cue is unchanged. This is the claim
layer's "intervention on the response" made concrete: same cue, blocked response.
investigations.title: Intervention: block the response
investigations.objective:
If the chemotactic response is blocked (lambda -> 0) while the cue is still
secreted, is recruitment abolished?
investigations.claim:
Blocking the chemotactic response abolishes recruitment: the recruitment index
stays at 0 (mean approach ~0), despite the cue being present.

investigations.name: recruitment-receptor-baseline
investigations.description:
The receptor-level realization of the chemotactic-recruitment claim. Where
recruitment-baseline gives every responder a hardcoded, always-on
chemotactic bias, this study makes the response emergent: each responder
carries a per-cell ReceptorSubcell that reads the local cue concentration
and computes fractional receptor occupancy via a Hill relation (kd, hill,
conc_scale, activate_occupancy). Only once occupancy crosses threshold does
a responder flip from naive (type 2, non-chemotaxing) to activated (type 3,
chemotaxing) -- see
pbg_cpm_studies.composites.chemotaxis_receptor.recruitment_receptor. The
receptor's Kd is not a free-fit parameter: it is the CXCL8 monomer-CXCR1
affinity reported in Nasser et al. 2009 (2.9 nM), so activation is
calibrated to a real receptor-ligand pair rather than an arbitrary lambda.
The Kd calibration is recorded as a parameter (model_settings below), not
as a literature_target on the recruitment-index test -- recruitment index
is a 0-1 fraction, and a Kd-valued target on that test would corrupt any
divergence_factor computed from it.
investigations.title: Receptor realization: cue + receptor-gated response recruits
investigations.objective:
Does a receptor-level realization of chemotactic recruitment -- where each
responder activates from naive to chemotaxing only once its per-cell
receptor-occupancy Hill relation crosses threshold -- reproduce the
baseline recruitment claim, using a cited receptor Kd instead of a
hand-tuned chemotaxis strength?
investigations.claim:
Cue + receptor-gated response recruits: across 5 seeds the final
recruitment index is 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882), above the 0.5 pass
threshold, with responder activation gated by a receptor Kd cited to
Nasser 2009 rather than a hand-tuned chemotaxis strength.

investigations.name: recruitment-receptor-blocked
investigations.description:
The intervention arm of the receptor-level realization, paired with
recruitment-receptor-baseline. The world and receptor wiring are identical
to the baseline -- same cue, same per-cell ReceptorSubcell computing Hill
occupancy against the same cited Kd (2.9 nM, Nasser et al. 2009) -- except
the activated type's chemotaxis lambda is forced to 0 in
chemotaxis_receptor.build_receptor_spec, the receptor-realization analogue
of pharmacologically blocking the response downstream of receptor binding.
As in the baseline, the Kd is recorded as a calibrated parameter
(model_settings below), not as a literature_target on the recruitment-index
test.
investigations.title: Receptor realization: blocking the response abolishes recruitment
investigations.objective:
In the receptor-level realization, if the activated response is forced off
(blocked=True, zeroing the activated-type chemotaxis lambda even for cells
that cross the receptor-occupancy activation threshold) while the cue is
still secreted, is recruitment abolished?
investigations.claim:
Blocking the response downstream of receptor activation abolishes
recruitment: the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467),
below the 0.1 pass threshold, despite the cue being present and receptors
still able to bind ligand.

investigations.name: vacancy_cavity
investigations.description: Reproduction of the Fig 28+ example from Glazier & Graner (Phys. Rev. E 47, 2128, 1993). Exact parameters: J_ll=14, J_dd=2, J_ld=11, J_lM=16, J_dM=16 (gamma_ld=+3, gamma_lM=+9, gamma_dM=+15); T=5.0, lambda=1.0, target A_l=20.0, A_d=40.0. Initial condition: equilibrated_random. Figures reproduced: Fig 28.
investigations.title: Vacancy nucleation (cavity)
investigations.objective: With unequal target areas (A_l=20, A_d=40) and vacancy nucleation allowed, does a light-cell-lined central cavity form?
investigations.claim: A light-cell-lined medium cavity nucleates within the aggregate (Fig 28); reproduced approximately (the paper notes this case is delicate).
